newsitem.title: NIGER: Police break march amid spreading unrest in Niger.
newsitem.headline: Police break march amid spreading unrest in Niger.

text.p: Police in the West African state of Niger fired teargas on Saturday to disperse hundreds of opposition supporters gathering in the capital Niamey for a pro-democracy protest, witnesses said.
Opposition militants set up barricades of burning tyres in several districts of the dusty Sahelian city and tension was reported in a number of provincial towns.

Witnesses said armed police later surrounded the Niamey homes of Niger's three main opposition leaders, including former civilian president Mahamane Ousmane and chief opposition spokesman Mahamadou Issoufou.
The three were at home but police prevented people from leaving or entering the houses, they said.

Opposition leaders said police used live ammunition in the clash and at least one protester was shot. There was no police comment, but a French radio correspondent reported from the scene that several people were wounded.
The march was part of opposition pressure on President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, a former coup leader, who is accused of legalising his rule through rigged elections.
Authorities had banned Saturday's march, citing mounting insecurity in the capital and other parts of the country, which borders Nigeria to the north.
Tension was also reported high in the interior, notably in opposition strongholds in the second city of Zinder and in the remote northeastern town of Diffa.
In the capital riot police massed early on Saturday to block a march on parliament called by an eight-party opposition alliance denouncing presidential elections in July.
Mainassara seized power in January 1996, saying he wanted to end a political deadlock between the then elected president Ousmane and his prime minister, who was from a different party.

Mainassara won presidential elections in July after scrapping the independent electoral commission in mid-poll. The opposition boycotted parliamentary elections in November after failing to secure cancellation of the July result.
The capital and the interior have been gripped by armed attacks, some suspected to be political.

A French woman was shot dead in the capital last Monday by suspected minority Touaregs whose armed elements have remained active despite an accord to end a revolt against the central government. It appeared the attackers were after her vehicle.
Several foreign tourists have been attacked in Niamey and in the provincial town of Agadez in recent weeks.
An official statement on state radio on Friday said: "Be it be known by each and everyone that the government will in no way tolerate a political ochestration of insecurity."
